After these things, Jesus showed himself again to the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias. He showed himself this way: Simon Peter and Thomas, called Didymus, and Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, and Zebedee’s sons, and two alloi from among his disciples were together. Simon Peter says to them, “I’m going fishing.” They say to him, “We’re coming too, with you.” They went out and got into the boat, and that night they caught nothing. By then morning had come, and Jesus stood on the shore. Yet the disciples did not ēdeisan that it was Jesus. So Jesus says to them, “Children, you don’t have any fish to eat, do you?” They answered him, “No.” He said to them, “Throw the net to the right side of the boat, and you will find.” So they threw it, and they could no longer pull it in because of the number of fish. Then that disciple whom Jesus ēgapa says to Peter, “It is the Lord!” So Simon Peter, hearing that it was the Lord, tied his outer garment around himself, for he was naked, and threw himself into the sea. But the alloi disciples came in the small boat, for they were not far from the shore, but about two hundred cubits away, dragging the net of fish. So when they stepped onto land, they blepoysin a charcoal fire there, and fish lying on it, and bread. Jesus says to them, “Bring some of the fish you just caught.” So Simon Peter went up and hauled the net onto the shore, full of 153 large fish. And although there were so many, the net did not tear. Jesus says to them, “Come, have breakfast.” But none of the disciples dared to ask him, “Who are you?” eidotes that he is the Lord. Jesus comes and takes the bread and gives it to them, and the fish in the same way. This was now the third time Jesus appeared to the disciples after being raised from the dead.

So when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus says to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you agapas me more than these?” He says to him, “Yes, Lord, you oidas that I philō you.” He says to him, “Feed my lambs.” He says to him again, a second time, “Simon, son of John, do you agapas me?” He says to him, “Yes, Lord, you oidas that I philō you.” He says to him, “Tend my sheep.” He says to him for the third time, “Simon, son of John, do you phileis me?” Peter was saddened because he said to him for the third time, “Do you phileis me?” And he says to him, “Lord, you oidas everything; you ginōskeis that I philō you.” He says to him, “Feed my sheep.” “Truly, truly, I tell you, when you were neōteros , you used to fasten your belt yourself and walk where you wanted. But when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and allos will fasten your belt and carry you where you do not want to go.” He said this to indicate by what kind of death he would glorify God. And after saying this, he says to him, “Follow me.”

Turning around, Peter blepei the disciple whom Jesus ēgapa following, who had also leaned against his chest at dinner and said, “Lord, who is the one handing you over?” So when Peter saw him, he says to Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?” Jesus says to him, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.” So this logos spread among the brothers, that that disciple would not die. But Jesus did not tell him that he would not die, but, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?”
